newsitem.title: USA: Air Force find human remains at A-10 crash site.
newsitem.headline: Air Force find human remains at A-10 crash site.

text.p: Authorities said Friday they had recovered "human remains" at the crash site of a missing A-10 warplane in Colorado.
Air Force Maj. Gen. Nels Running told reporters investigators planned to perform DNA tests on the remains to determine if they belonged to the pilot, Capt. Craig Button.
Running declined to specify what remains were found by the rescue team but he said results from identification tests should be known within 72 hours.
"What we found was fragmentary human remains," he said. "We are positive they are human remains, we are not positive whose human remains they are."

The A-10 attack aircraft disappeared during a routine training mission April 2 and Air Force officials have been at a loss to explain why Button, 32, veered northeast into Colorado, some 850 miles away (1360 km) from a training exercise.
Button's plane was carrying four 500-pound (225-kg) Mark 82 conventional bombs.
